title: ChatGPT Wallet lets OpenAI’s Dots agents make purchases for you
content:
After launching its Dots AI agents platform earlier this year, OpenAI is launching a wallet for the agents. ChatGPT Wallet is rolling out starting today for ChatGPT Pro subscribers in the US aged 18 and older using a US billing address and “eligible US-issued American Express, Chase, Mastercard and Visa cards.”
ChatGPT Wallet lets OpenAI’s Dots agents make purchases for you
OpenAI says ChatGPT Wallet won’t share your actual credit card info with its AI agents.
After adding a card to the wallet, your Dots agents can use it to buy things in response to your prompts, but they’ll check in with you each time before checking out. OpenAI’s support page says every purchase with ChatGPT Wallet requires a security check with biometric verification like Face ID or a fingerprint scan.
After you review the AI agent’s purchase and sign off on it, OpenAI says that, similar to using tap to pay, Apple Pay, or Google Wallet, it substitutes your credit card details with a payment token, so your actual card info isn’t shared with your Dots agent or the business you’re buying from. Eventually, OpenAI says it expects “users to be able to delegate purchases entirely to their agent by setting clear parameters—such as spending limits, purchase categories, or time periods—and pre-approve those purchases.”
ChatGPT Wallet might not work everywhere. Some retailers have restrictions on AI agents or block them altogether. Earlier this year, Amazon blocked Meta’s Muse agents. OpenAI says that in order for agents to use ChatGPT Wallet, “websites need to ensure agents are not inadvertently blocked, and payment and risk systems need to recognize legitimate purchases made by agents.”

report.summary: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Wallet for US Pro users, letting Dots AI agents make purchases with biometric approval and tokenized card details.
report.background: OpenAI's move reflects AI agents shifting from answering questions to acting on users' behalf. After launching Dots agents earlier this year, OpenAI is adding payments, the missing link for agentic commerce. Digital wallets like Apple Pay and Google Pay already use tokenization to avoid sharing card numbers, and OpenAI is borrowing that trust model. The challenge is merchant acceptance: some retailers restrict or block AI agents, and Amazon earlier blocked Meta's Muse agents. Payment networks and risk systems must distinguish legitimate agent purchases from fraud. OpenAI also faces questions about liability, consent, spending controls, and data privacy. The wallet is initially limited to US Pro subscribers, signaling a cautious rollout as OpenAI tests whether consumers will trust agents with checkout decisions.
key_points: ChatGPT Wallet is rolling out to US ChatGPT Pro subscribers aged 18+ with a US billing address and eligible US-issued American Express, Chase, Mastercard, or Visa cards. The limited launch signals a cautious first step into agentic payments rather than a broad consumer rollout.

Users add a card to the wallet, then Dots agents can make purchases in response to prompts. Every checkout requires the user to review and approve the purchase, with biometric verification such as Face ID or a fingerprint scan, so agents cannot buy things silently.

OpenAI says the wallet uses payment tokenization, similar to Apple Pay or Google Wallet. The actual credit card details are not shared with the Dots agent or the merchant; a token stands in for the card, reducing exposure if an agent or retailer is compromised.

OpenAI expects a future where users can delegate purchases entirely by setting parameters like spending limits, purchase categories, and time periods, then pre-approving transactions. That would move the wallet from assisted checkout toward more autonomous agent commerce.

The wallet may not work everywhere. Some retailers restrict or block AI agents; Amazon earlier blocked Meta's Muse agents. OpenAI says websites must avoid inadvertently blocking agents, and payment and risk systems need to recognize legitimate agent-initiated purchases.
report.impact: For the AI industry, ChatGPT Wallet is a milestone in agentic commerce: it moves agents from recommendations to transactions and pressures payment networks, merchants, and platforms to support agent identity, consent, and risk controls. Developers will need payment APIs, tokenization, approval flows, and merchant integrations that treat agents as a distinct buyer type. Regular users get convenience but must manage approvals, spending limits, fraud risk, and privacy; adoption depends on merchant acceptance and trust. If successful, the wallet could accelerate competition with Google, Apple, Meta, and payment firms, while fragmentation and retailer blocking remain near-term obstacles.
report.tools: Watch OpenAI's Dots platform and ChatGPT Wallet support pages for rollout details. Compare with tokenization systems from Apple Pay and Google Wallet. For merchant and developer infrastructure, follow Stripe's agentic commerce tools, Visa Intelligent Commerce, and Mastercard Agent Pay, which are building agent-specific payment rails. Open-source agent frameworks such as LangChain and CrewAI can help developers prototype consent, spending-limit, and approval workflows, though they are not payment wallets themselves.
